workload.explanationTitle: Explanation of terms and risk scoring
workload.riskScoreDescription: The risk score (0–100) is calculated as the sum of five categories: severity, exploitation evidence, exposure, environment context, and actionability. Higher value means it's more urgent.

vulnerabilityDetail.descriptionShowMore: See the rest of the description...
vulnerabilityDetail.noRiskFactors: No risk factors are identified for this vulnerability.

filter.showingLimited: Showing {showing} of {total}. Search to narrow down.

descriptions.severity: Based on the standardised technical severity rating (CVSSv3) of the vulnerability — independent of context.
descriptions.exploitation_evidence: We search metadata from multiple sources for traces of known or active exploitation — for example whether public proof-of-concept exploits exist, or whether the vulnerability has been confirmed actively exploited against others.
descriptions.exposure: Considers whether the application is reachable from the internet, only internally within Nav, or has no network access. An exposed application increases risk considerably.
descriptions.environment: Evaluates which environment the application runs in, and whether the vulnerability has been left unaddressed for a long time. Production environments and older findings are weighted more heavily.
descriptions.actionability: Looks at whether a fix is available for the vulnerability, and whether it is known to be used in ransomware attacks. Available fixes increase priority; a missing fix reduces it.

complianceMeasurement.title: How we measure security status
complianceMeasurement.calculatedAt: Calculated {timestamp} ({timeZone}). This is not the last data collection time.
complianceMeasurement.intro: The three metrics describe the latest calculated situation. The monthly boxes summarise historical days, not whether you need to act now. All application environments are included; deployments of the same application in different environments count separately.
complianceMeasurement.historyColours: Each box uses the most frequent daily status in that month. A check mark means on track, an exclamation mark means needs attention, and a cross means act now. Ties use the worse colour: red before yellow before green. Most frequent does not necessarily mean more than half of the days. Grey means no recorded days. Hover, focus or tap a box to see the month, day counts and on-track percentage.
complianceMeasurement.historyFormula: The on-track percentage in the tooltip = days when all three metrics were green ÷ recorded days × 100. Every recorded calendar day has equal weight, including weekends. Percentages are rounded to the nearest whole percentage point. The box colour uses the most frequent status, not percentage thresholds or an average of colour scores.
complianceMeasurement.dailyStatus: A day is on track (green) only when all three metrics are green. It needs attention (yellow) if at least one metric is yellow and none is red. It requires action (red) if any metric is red. The day counts show the full distribution, so earlier problems remain visible even after recovery.
complianceMeasurement.historyCoverage: We show up to {months} calendar months, oldest first, limited to available history. A day counts if a tracked application was present during any part of the evaluated day, outside recorded absences. Days before tracking began, or with no application presence at all, are excluded from both the colour counts and the percentage. A month without recorded days is grey and has no percentage. The current month includes only elapsed dates through today.
complianceMeasurement.dailyTiming: Dates use {timeZone}. Historical trend and maintenance are evaluated at the end of each day; today uses the calculation time. Exposure includes applications that were overdue at any time during the day, even if fixed later that day. This also applies to today's exposure status, while its application list shows only currently unresolved overdue findings. Today's result can change before the day ends.
complianceMeasurement.deadlines: Deadlines run from the recorded discovery time: {critical} workdays for CRITICAL vulnerabilities and {nonCritical} calendar months for all other severities, including unknown severity. This uses severity, not the prioritisation risk score or bucket.
complianceMeasurement.exposureRules: Green: no applications past deadline. Yellow: exactly one application past deadline, with every overdue finding less than {workdays} workdays overdue. Red: at least two applications past deadline, or any finding at least {workdays} workdays overdue. Multiple overdue findings in one application count as one application.
complianceMeasurement.workdays: Workdays mean Monday to Friday. Public holidays are not excluded. Deadlines retain the discovery time of day, and overdue workdays are counted from the deadline by the SLA calculation.
complianceMeasurement.trendWindow: At each evaluation time we compare new vulnerability discoveries with resolution events in the preceding {days} days. These are counts of findings and resolution events, not application counts or risk scores. A finding resolved again after reappearing can contribute another resolution event; reappearance itself is not counted as a new discovery.
complianceMeasurement.trendStable: The trend is stable when |new − resolved| ≤ {ratio} × max(new, resolved), including when both counts are zero. Otherwise it is worse when new exceeds resolved, and improving when resolved exceeds new.
complianceMeasurement.trendRules: Stable or improving is green. Worse is yellow when no applications were overdue that day, and red when at least one was. Until the team has a full {days}-day tracking window, the trend is treated as stable; that does not prove improvement.
complianceMeasurement.trendChart: The small chart shows applications with overdue findings at each month end, and at calculation time for the current month. It provides backlog context; it is not the rolling-window calculation that determines the trend status.
complianceMeasurement.maintenanceAge: An application is up to date when its latest recorded deployment is no more than {days} whole 24-hour days old. The calculation measures deployment age, not whether a new image was actually built.
complianceMeasurement.maintenanceRules: Green: all counted applications are up to date. Yellow: at least {ratio}, but not all, are up to date. Red: less than {ratio} are up to date. When no applications can be counted, this metric is green; that is not proof of completed maintenance.
complianceMeasurement.maintenanceCoverage: Only applications present at the evaluation time are counted. If an application has no deployment history, its first-tracked time is used as the age reference. If deployment history exists but contains no deployment before that time, the application is excluded from that day's maintenance denominator.
complianceMeasurement.levels: These badges describe the current consecutive off-track period, not the monthly percentage. There is no badge when all three metrics are green. Chronic means at least {months} calendar months continuously off track, or all three metrics red. Otherwise, ongoing means at least {workdays} workdays off track, or at least two metrics red. Remaining off-track teams are new. Workdays in the consecutive period include its starting date when it is a weekday.
complianceMeasurement.dataLimitations: History is reconstructed from stored vulnerability lifecycles, recorded deployments and application presence, not immutable daily snapshots. Missing collection runs within a tracked period are not separately detected or excluded. Current severity data and current thresholds are applied when reconstructing history, so historical results can change after data corrections or configuration changes.
complianceMeasurement.freshness: The calculation timestamp tells you when these results were computed, not when Nais was last collected. Results depend on stored synchronisation data and may lag behind a deployment or fix. Reloading recalculates from the available data; it does not guarantee a completed data collection.
